formation.title: The Yavana Restoration
formation.text:
For centuries the Yavana name has echoed through Indian chronicles: the Greeks who came from beyond the mountains, who struck coins in two languages and worshipped the Enlightened One in marble temples. Now a Sindhi Buddhist ruler has dared what no one thought possible: the revival of the Indo-Greek kingdom.

From Thatta on the Indus delta to Peshawar in the shadow of the Khyber Pass, the ancient Yavana domains answer to a single throne once more. But what manner of state shall this be? The phalanx drills in the courtyards of Gandharan monasteries, and merchants strike bilingual coins in workshops that smell of incense and olive oil.

Two paths lie before the restored Yavana Empire: one looking to the military genius of Alexander's heirs, the other to the philosophical synthesis that made these kingdoms unique among all the world's civilizations.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We shall revive the phalanx that conquered half the world

modifiers.name: Phalanx Reborn
modifiers.text: The sarissa-armed phalanx has risen again in the lands between the Indus and the Hindu Kush. What Alexander's successors brought east, we have made our own.

options.text: Our dharma bridges East and West in wisdom

modifiers.name: Dharma of the Yavana
modifiers.text: Where Greek philosophy meets Buddhist wisdom, a new civilization blossoms. Our coins bear two scripts, our temples two traditions, and our scholars speak to all the world.

advances.name: Phalanx Revival
advances.text: The Macedonian phalanx, brought to India by Alexander's successors, is drilled anew in the courtyards of Sindh. Heavy infantry armed with the sarissa pike form the backbone of the Yavana army.

advances.name: Gandhara Monasteries
advances.text: Buddhist monasteries built in the Greek architectural style serve as centers of learning and worship, preserving texts in both Greek and Prakrit.

advances.name: Bilingual Administration
advances.text: State documents are issued in both Greek and Prakrit, ensuring that the Hellenistic bureaucracy and Indian subjects can communicate without barriers.

advances.name: Elephant Corps
advances.text: The Indo-Greek kingdoms adopted Indian war elephants with enthusiasm, armoring them and mounting fighting platforms atop these living fortresses.

advances.name: Indus Trade Networks
advances.text: Control of the Indus River and the mountain passes connecting India to Central Asia gives the Yavana state command over some of the most lucrative trade routes in the ancient world.

advances.name: Bilingual Coinage
advances.text: Coins struck with Greek on one face and Kharosthi on the other, a hallmark of Indo-Greek civilization that facilitates trade across linguistic boundaries.

advances.name: Gajasena Tradition
advances.text: The formalized doctrine of elephant warfare, training beasts and mahouts together in coordinated tactics that maximize the terrifying impact of a charging elephant line.

advances.name: Milindapanha Dialogues
advances.text: The philosophical dialogues between Greek rationalism and Buddhist contemplation, following the model of King Menander's legendary exchanges with the monk Nagasena.

event.title: The Questions of Milinda
event.text:
In the ancient text known as the Milindapanha, the Greek king Menander (called Milinda in Pali) engaged the Buddhist monk Nagasena in a series of profound philosophical dialogues. The king asked the deepest questions about the nature of the self, of karma, of existence itself, and the monk answered with parables and razor-sharp logic.

This tradition of dialogue between Greek rational inquiry and Buddhist contemplative wisdom was the intellectual foundation of the Indo-Greek kingdoms. Now our scholars have revived these methods, hosting public debates between philosophers of every school in the gymnasia and viharas of our cities.

Shall we emphasize the spiritual dimension of this tradition, or its contribution to rational knowledge?

options.text: Let the dialogue illuminate the path to nirvana

modifiers.name: Questions of Milinda
modifiers.text: In the tradition of King Menander's dialogues with the monk Nagasena, our court embraces the union of reason and enlightenment.

options.text: Let reason be our guide to understanding the world

modifiers.name: Rational Inquiry
modifiers.text: The Greek method of systematic questioning applied to the mysteries of the world yields discoveries that neither tradition alone could achieve.

advances.name: Gandhara Art School
advances.text: Greek sculptural techniques applied to Buddhist religious subjects, creating the first human representations of the Buddha and establishing an artistic tradition that will spread across all of Asia.

event.title: The Gandhara Art School
event.text:
In the workshops of Gandhara, something extraordinary has emerged. Our sculptors, trained in the Greek tradition of naturalistic human representation, have turned their skills to Buddhist subjects. For the first time in history, the Buddha is depicted not as an abstract symbol (a wheel, a tree, a set of footprints) but as a serene human figure draped in a toga-like robe, his hair arranged in waves reminiscent of Apollo.

These images carry an emotional power that purely symbolic art cannot match. Pilgrims weep before the compassionate face of the Enlightened One. The art is spreading along trade routes in every direction, and with it the fame of Yavana civilization.

options.text: Our art shall carry the dharma to the ends of the earth

advances.name: Strategoi Governance
advances.text: The Hellenistic system of provincial governance through military-civil strategoi, adapted to Indian conditions and providing both frontier defense and administrative efficiency.

advances.name: Hellenistic Gymnasium
advances.text: The Greek gymnasium tradition of physical training combined with philosophical education, creating citizens trained in both body and mind.

advances.name: Combined Arms Doctrine
advances.text: The systematic coordination of infantry phalanx, war elephants, mounted archers, and light skirmishers into a single flexible fighting force, neither purely Greek nor purely Indian.

event.title: The Fourfold Array
event.text:
The Milinda Panha describes Menander's army as a fourfold force: elephants, cavalry, archers, and foot soldiers. Our generals have formalized this ancient doctrine into a comprehensive system of combined arms warfare.

The phalanx holds the center with their sarissas, an unbreakable wall of iron points. On the flanks, mounted archers harass and screen. Behind the lines, war elephants wait in reserve: living siege towers that shatter enemy formations when committed at the decisive moment. Skirmishers and light troops fill the gaps, maintaining contact between the four arms.

No army in India fights like this. It is neither purely Greek nor purely Indian, but something new, and devastating.

options.text: Let the fourfold array carry all before it

modifiers.name: Fourfold Array
modifiers.text: Infantry, cavalry, elephants, and archers operate as a single coordinated force in the Hellenistic tradition of combined arms.

advances.name: Syncretic Markets
advances.text: Marketplaces where Greek commercial law meets Indian trading customs, overseen by agoranomoi who enforce fair weights and measures in a bilingual trading environment.

advances.name: Dharma of Statecraft
advances.text: Buddhist ethical principles applied to Hellenistic governance, a philosophy of just rule that draws on both Ashoka's edicts and Aristotle's Politics.

advances.name: Taxila University Tradition
advances.text: The ancient university at Taxila, where scholars from across Asia gathered to study medicine, mathematics, and philosophy, is revived as the intellectual heart of the Yavana state.

advances.name: Hippotoxotai Tradition
advances.text: Mounted archers combining Greek horsemanship with the composite bow techniques of the Central Asian steppe, providing the fast-moving cavalry arm of the Yavana military.

advances.name: Greco-Buddhist Patronage
advances.text: State-sponsored religious syncretism where Greek deities are identified with Buddhist and Hindu figures, and temples serve worshippers of multiple traditions under one roof.

advances.name: Imperial Administration
advances.text: The centralized Hellenistic bureaucracy of eparchs, dioiketai, and hyparchoi adapted to govern a subcontinental empire, collecting taxes and dispensing justice in two languages.

advances.name: Silk Road Entrepot
advances.text:
The Yavana Empire sits at the junction of overland routes from China, sea routes from the Mediterranean, and river routes down the Indus, a position of extraordinary commercial power.

Available in: Yavana Mint

advances.name: Syntagma Reform
advances.text: The syntagma (a tactical unit of the reformed phalanx) becomes the basis of a professional standing army, drilled to Hellenistic standards and paid from the imperial treasury.

advances.name: Universal Dharma
advances.text: A mature philosophy of religious tolerance rooted in Buddhist compassion and Greek cosmopolitanism, offering citizenship and dignity to all peoples regardless of creed.

advances.name: Standing Army Reforms
advances.text: The transition from seasonal levy warfare to a permanent professional force maintained year-round, following the Hellenistic model of paid soldiers owing loyalty to the state.

advances.name: Gandharan Renaissance
advances.text: A flowering of artistic production as Gandharan techniques are applied to sculpture, painting, metalwork, and architecture across the empire.

advances.name: Grand Vihara Network
advances.text:
A network of monastic universities spanning the empire, where monks copy texts, teach mathematics and medicine, and serve as the intellectual backbone of the state.

Unlocks: Birch Bark Scriptorium

advances.name: Enlightened Syncretism
advances.text: The philosophical culmination of centuries of Greco-Buddhist dialogue, a mature intellectual tradition that draws freely on Greek, Indian, and Central Asian thought.

advances.name: Modern Phalanx
advances.text:
The ancient phalanx tradition evolves into disciplined line infantry capable of volley fire, maintaining the Hellenistic emphasis on formation discipline in the age of gunpowder.

Unlocks: Phalangites of the Line

advances.name: Industrial Crossroads
advances.text: The geographic position that once made the Yavana state a trade crossroads now drives industrial development, as raw materials flow in from every direction.

advances.name: Yavana Legacy
advances.text:
The enduring legacy of the Indo-Greek synthesis, a civilization that proved East and West could merge into something greater than either alone.

Available in: Birch Bark Scriptorium

destiny.name: Reclaim Bactria
destiny.text: The Yavana Empire must reclaim the ancient Greco-Bactrian heartland beyond the Hindu Kush (Kabul, Kandahar, and Ghazni) to restore the full extent of Alexander's eastern inheritance.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25
Own Kābul, or a subject owns it
Own Kandahār, or a subject owns it
Own Ġaznī, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Return to Bactria
event.text:
Our armies have crossed the Hindu Kush and planted the Yavana standard in the ancient cities of Bactria. Kabul, where Alexander himself once camped. Kandahar, which bears his name in corrupted form. Ghazni, gateway to the Iranian plateau.

For the first time since the fall of the Greco-Bactrian kingdom, a single Hellenistic power commands both the Indus valley and the Afghan highlands. The mountain passes that connect India to Central Asia are ours. The trade routes that carried Greek culture eastward and Buddhist wisdom westward now flow through our customs houses.

This is only the beginning.

options.text: The mountains answer to the phalanx once more

destiny.name: The Bactrian March
destiny.text: Push the sarissa-armed phalanx northward to Balkh and Herat, the great cities of ancient Bactria, and to Termez, where a Greek fortress once kept the crossing of the Oxus.

conditions.text: Path of the Phalanx
Own Balkh, or a subject owns it
Own Herāt, or a subject owns it
Own Termez, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Bactrian March
event.text:
Balkh, the ancient capital of Bactria (the 'mother of cities' as the Arabs called it), flies the Yavana banner. Herat, jewel of Khorasan, has fallen to our phalanx. The sarissa-armed infantry that first appeared on these plains two millennia ago under Alexander have returned.

Our strategoi govern provinces that stretch from the Indus delta to the gates of Persia. The combined arms doctrine of elephant, cavalry, and phalanx has proven itself against every foe. In the bazaars of Balkh, merchants strike bilingual coins bearing Greek legends and Kharosthi script.

The reconquest of Greater Bactria is complete. What remains is to decide how far the phalanx shall march.

options.text: Let the sarissa carry our standard further still

destiny.name: The Sarissa Empire
destiny.text: Carry the Hellenistic military tradition to Samarkand and to Khujand, the farthest of Alexander's cities, in the north and to Delhi in the east, forging a continental empire held together by the unbreakable phalanx.

conditions.text: Own Samarkand, or a subject owns it
Own Delhi, or a subject owns it
Own Khujand, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 50

event.title: The Sarissa Empire
event.text:
From Samarkand's fabled markets to the walls of Delhi, the Yavana phalanx has carved an empire that dwarfs anything the original Indo-Greek kings achieved. Menander would weep with pride.

Our army is the finest in Asia: disciplined infantry, screening horse archers, thundering elephant charges, all coordinated by strategoi trained in the combined arms tradition. But even the greatest army requires a doctrine for its continued growth.

Shall we expand our forces through mass levies and rapid maneuver, overwhelming our enemies with numbers and speed? Or shall we invest in professional training and defensive fortifications, making every soldier worth ten of the enemy?

options.text: Flood the field with sarissas and elephants

modifiers.name: Tide of Sarissas
modifiers.text: Mass levies and rapid maneuver overwhelm our enemies with the sheer weight of the Yavana phalanx.

options.text: Train each soldier to fight with iron discipline

modifiers.name: Iron Discipline
modifiers.text: Professional training and fortified positions make every Yavana soldier worth ten of the enemy.

destiny.name: Alexander's Dream
destiny.text: Reach the Ganges at Varanasi and Patna, the goal Alexander himself was denied, and take Ayodhya, the Saketa that the Yavana kings once besieged. With a full treasury, the conquest he began is completed.

conditions.text: Own Varanasi, or a subject owns it
Own Patna, or a subject owns it
Own Ayodhya, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 3000
Prestige at least 75

event.title: Alexander's Dream Fulfilled
event.text:
The Ganges. Alexander wept because he had no more worlds to conquer, or so the legend says. In truth, his army mutinied at the Hyphasis, refusing to march further east. What Alexander could not achieve, the Yavana Empire has accomplished.

Our banners fly over Varanasi, holiest city of the Hindus, and Patna, the ancient Pataliputra where Chandragupta Maurya once received Seleucid ambassadors. The sarissa and the war elephant have carried Greek arms to the heart of India.

This is the apex of Hellenistic military power. How shall we cement this achievement for eternity?

modifiers.name: Phalanx Ascendant
modifiers.text: The Yavana military machine operates with relentless efficiency, launching campaigns faster and sustaining them longer than any rival.

options.text: We shall dictate terms to the world

modifiers.name: World Conqueror
modifiers.text: The Yavana Empire dictates terms to the world from a position of overwhelming military supremacy.

destiny.name: The Light of Bamiyan
destiny.text: Secure the great Buddha statues of Bamiyan, fill the treasury and endow three viharas of the Gandharan kind, to build a civilization worthy of both Greek philosophy and Buddhist wisdom.

conditions.text: Path of Dharma
Own Bamyan, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 1000
At least 3 of our locations have a Gandhara Vihara

event.title: The Light of Bamiyan
event.text:
The great Buddhas of Bamiyan gaze down upon our soldiers with serene compassion as the Yavana standard is raised before them. These colossal statues, carved from the living rock of the Hindu Kush, represent everything our civilization aspires to be: the marriage of Greek artistic mastery and Buddhist spiritual depth.

Our scholars have established a new vihara in Bamiyan's shadow, where monks debate philosophy in Greek and Prakrit, and sculptors trained in the Gandharan tradition carve images that will inspire pilgrims for centuries to come.

The path of dharma stretches onward.

options.text: May the light of wisdom illuminate all lands

destiny.name: The Silk Dharma
destiny.text: Draw silk into the capital's markets and rebuild Taxila, the old city of learning near Rawalpindi, until the Yavana realm becomes the intellectual and commercial crossroads of Asia.

conditions.text: The capital

children.text: Silk is produced in the market
Silk is traded in the market

conditions.text: Owns Taxila (Rawalpindi) and its development is at least 45
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Silk Dharma
event.text:
Caravans bearing Chinese silk arrive at our capital's markets alongside merchants carrying Roman glass, Central Asian horses, and Indian spices. The Yavana Empire sits at the crossroads of the world's greatest trade routes, and our prosperity reflects it.

Our cities grow. Our scholars multiply. The viharas and gymnasia that line our roads produce monks, philosophers, physicians, and merchants in equal measure. But prosperity creates its own choices.

Shall we invest this wealth in the material wellbeing of our subjects, reducing unrest and building a contented populace? Or shall we use it to draw scholars and diplomats from across the world, making our court the most cosmopolitan in Asia?

options.text: Let our people prosper under the dharma

modifiers.name: Dharma of Prosperity
modifiers.text: Buddhist ethics of contentment and good governance reduce unrest and separatism across the empire.

options.text: Let the world's scholars gather at our court

modifiers.name: Cosmopolitan Court
modifiers.text: The Yavana court draws scholars and diplomats from across the known world, integrating vassal states through cultural magnetism.

destiny.name: The Universal Light
destiny.text: Extend Greco-Buddhist learning to Mathura and Ujjain, the sacred cities of the Gangetic heartland. Raise Mathura, city of the sculptors, to twice its size and open Agora-Bazaars in four towns, whose trade will fund the greatest syncretic civilization in history.

conditions.text: Owns Mathura and its development is at least 64
Own Ujjain, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75
Owns a location with

event.title: The Universal Light
event.text:
Mathura, sacred to both Buddhists and Hindus, and Ujjain, the ancient astronomical capital of India, both now shelter Yavana universities where Greek logic meets Buddhist meditation and Hindu mathematics. Our empire has become what no other civilization in history has achieved: a living synthesis of East and West.

Scholars travel from the Mediterranean to study at our academies. Our bilingual texts are copied in monasteries from Sri Lanka to Sogdia. The Gandharan art tradition has spread the image of the Buddha across half the world. And in our courts, philosophers of every school debate freely under the protection of a state that values wisdom above dogma.

This is the culmination of the Yavana vision. How shall we preserve it?

modifiers.name: Living Synthesis
modifiers.text: The fusion of Greek and Buddhist intellectual traditions produces a civilization that attracts the world's finest minds.

options.text: Through tolerance that embraces all faiths

modifiers.name: Tolerant Empire
modifiers.text: A state founded on religious tolerance and syncretic wisdom, where all faiths are welcomed and none are persecuted.

units.name: Pezhetairoi
units.text: Heavy infantry armed with the sarissa pike, reviving the Macedonian phalanx tradition that conquered the known world under Alexander.

units.name: Gajasena
units.text: Armored war elephants bearing fighting towers, combining Indian elephant husbandry with Greek military engineering to create the most terrifying weapon on the battlefield.

units.name: Thureophoroi
units.text: Versatile medium infantry carrying the thureos shield and armed with javelins and swords, trained to fight in both Greek formation and Indian skirmish tactics.

units.name: Hippotoxotai
units.text: Mounted archers combining Greek cavalry discipline with Central Asian composite bow techniques, swift raiders who harass enemy flanks and screen the army's advance.

units.name: Syntagma Guard
units.text: Elite professional heavy infantry of the reformed phalanx, paid soldiers drilled to fight as a single organism in the syntagma formation.

units.name: Phalangites of the Line
units.text: Musket infantry drilled in the close files of the old phalanx. The line holds under fire and volleys as one body, though it is slow to change front.

buildings.name: Gandhara Vihara
buildings.text: A Buddhist monastery built in the Greco-Buddhist architectural style, with Corinthian columns framing meditation halls and Greek-trained sculptors crafting images of the Buddha.

buildings.name: Yavana Mint
buildings.text: A coinage workshop striking the distinctive bilingual coins of the Yavana state: Greek legends on one face, Kharosthi on the other.

buildings.name: Hastisala
buildings.text: An elephant training and stabling compound where mahouts and beasts are trained together in the arts of war, maintaining the Yavana elephant corps.

buildings.name: Gymnasium
buildings.text: A Hellenistic training ground where citizens exercise the body and the mind, studying philosophy and rhetoric alongside wrestling and javelin-throwing.

buildings.name: Agora-Bazaar
buildings.text: A syncretic marketplace where Greek commercial practices and Indian trading customs merge under the watchful eye of bilingual market officials.

buildings.name: Birch Bark Scriptorium
buildings.text: A copying house of the vihara network, where monks write sutras and Greek treatises in Kharosthi and Greek on rolls of birch bark, as the scribes of Gandhara did.

buildings.name: Strategos Akademia
buildings.text: An elite military academy where commanders are trained in the combined arms doctrine of phalanx, elephant, and cavalry, producing strategoi worthy of Alexander's legacy.

buildings.name: Mahasanghika University
buildings.text: A great center of syncretic learning where Greek philosophy, Buddhist wisdom, and Hindu mathematics are studied together, producing scholars who bridge the intellectual traditions of East and West.

list.name: Eparchia Strategoi
list.text: The Indo-Greek satrapal governorship adapted from Achaemenid and Seleucid practice. Each eparchy was led by a strategos, a military governor who combined Hellenistic command authority with civil revenue powers. The Shinkot reliquary inscription names the meridarch Theodorus, and the Taxila copper-plate of Patika confirms a strategos serving under Indo-Greek hegemony. The institution centralizes royal authority through standing provincial commands at the cost of the hipparch landed cavalry caste.

list.name: Sangha Patronage
list.text: The royal endowment apparatus channelling crown revenue to the Buddhist order. Menander I's patronage of the sangha is recorded in the Milindapanha and physically attested in the Shinkot, Bajaur, and Bimaran reliquary inscriptions, where Indo-Greek officers and the king's household dedicate stupas and monastic gifts. Borrowing the Ashokan dhamma-mahamatra office, the apparatus places permanent royal officers within the Greco-Buddhist viharas to administer endowments and supervise discipline.

conditions.text: Any of

list.name: Polis-Asty Council
list.text: Hellenistic civic government applied to the Indo-Greek cities. Sagala, Taxila and Pushkalavati preserved the Greek polis form: a council (boule) of citizens, archons and astynomoi regulating markets, courts and citizen militias under royal hegemony. The civic mints struck Attic-weight tetradrachms with city marks, confirming corporate authority over coinage. Power flows to the urban merchant body, structurally weakening the rural cavalry-aristocracy.

list.name: Bilingual Chancery
list.text: The dual-script secretariat that produced parallel Greek and Karoshthi-Prakrit official text: on coin legends, royal decrees, reliquary dedications and revenue accounts. The Heliodorus pillar at Besnagar, the Reh inscription, and the obverse-reverse legends of every Indo-Greek tetradrachm document a working chancery whose scribes were trained in two scripts. The institution drives literacy into both the Greek garrison towns and the Indian countryside, but its costs fall on the urban merchant class that staffs it.
